documents.title: H&P - Admission, COPD Exacerbation
lines: HPI:
63 yo F with GOLD III COPD, ongoing 40 pack-yr tobacco use, presents at 01:20 with 3 days of worsening cough, thick yellow sputum and dyspnea at rest.
Home albuterol MDI used q2h today without relief. No fever chills. No chest pain. No leg swelling.
Somnolent on arrival, arousable to voice but falls asleep mid-sentence; wife reports this is new today.
ED course:
SpO2 89% at triage; 1L NC started, SpO2 92%.
Mild accessory muscle use noted at triage, resolved after first nebulizer; respiratory rate 22.
Three albuterol-ipratropium nebulizers given in the ED between 01:40 and 03:00 plus methylprednisolone 125 mg IV; persistent diffuse wheeze and dyspnea at rest afterward.
ABG at 03:15: pH 7.29, PaCO2 64, PaO2 58 on 4L.
PMH: COPD with 2 prior exacerbations in past yr, type 2 DM on metformin, GERD, osteoporosis.
Home meds: tiotropium 18 mcg daily, budesonide-formoterol 160/4.5 2 puffs BID, albuterol MDI prn, metformin 1000 mg BID, pantoprazole 40 mg daily, calcium-vit D.
Allergies: sulfa (rash).
Social: lives with wife, 1 flight of stairs at home, still smoking approx 1/2 ppd.
Exam:
T 37.1 HR 104 BP 148/82 RR 22 SpO2 92% on 1L NC.
Gen: drowsy, arouses to voice, answers in short phrases.
Lungs: diffuse expiratory wheeze bilaterally, prolonged expiratory phase, poor air movement at bases.
Abd: soft, nontender. Ext: no edema. Neuro: no asterixis, moves all 4, no focal deficit.
Labs: WBC 12.4, Hgb 13.1, Na 137, K 4.2, Cr 0.8, glucose 188, lactate 1.4.
CXR: hyperinflation, flattened diaphragms, no focal consolidation, no effusion.
Assessment/Plan:
1. Acute COPD exacerbation with acute hypercapnic respiratory acidosis - admit to stepdown, continuous pulse ox, titrate O2 to SpO2 88-92%.
2. Scheduled albuterol-ipratropium neb q4h with q2h prn; continue inhaled maintenance once more awake.
3. IV steroid: methylprednisolone 40 mg IV every 8 hours.
4. Azithromycin 500 mg IV x1 then 250 mg daily for purulent sputum.
5. Repeat ABG in 4 h; hold sedating meds given somnolence. Smoking cessation counseling, nicotine patch 14 mg offered.
6. DM: hold metformin, q6h POC glucose while on steroids.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - HD2
lines: Discharge dx: acute COPD exacerbation with transient hypercapnia, steroid-induced hyperglycemia.
Admitted HD1 at 04:10 from ED for dyspnea at rest, purulent sputum and drowsiness.
Hospital course:
SpO2 89% at triage; 1L NC started, SpO2 92%. Mild accessory muscle use noted at triage, resolved after first nebulizer; respiratory rate 22.
Three albuterol-ipratropium nebulizers given in the ED between 01:40 and 03:00 plus methylprednisolone 125 mg IV; persistent diffuse wheeze and dyspnea at rest afterward.
ABG at 03:15: pH 7.29, PaCO2 64, PaO2 58 on 4L. Somnolent on arrival, arousable to voice but falls asleep mid-sentence; wife reports this is new today.
Managed with controlled O2 to target SpO2 88-92%, scheduled bronchodilators and steroids. Repeat ABG HD1 09:40: pH 7.36, PaCO2 49, PaO2 71 on 2L. Mentation back to baseline by 11:00.
IV steroid: methylprednisolone 40 mg IV every 8 hours; glucose rose to 342 requiring insulin sliding scale. Glucose 166-198 by HD2 morning off IV steroid.
Weaned to room air HD2 07:00, SpO2 93% at rest and 91% after ambulating hallway with RN.
Discharge exam: alert, oriented, RR 18, scattered mild end-expiratory wheeze, clear speech in full sentences.
Discharge meds: prednisone 40 mg PO daily x 4 more days, azithromycin 250 mg daily x 3 more days, tiotropium 18 mcg daily, budesonide-formoterol 160/4.5 2 puffs BID, albuterol MDI q4h prn.
Resume metformin 1000 mg BID; check fingerstick glucose BID while on prednisone, call if readings above 300.
Nicotine patch 14 mg daily dispensed; cessation counseling given, quitline info provided.
Follow up with primary care in 5-7 days, pulmonary clinic in 3 weeks with spirometry.
Return precautions: worsening dyspnea, confusion or unusual sleepiness, fever, inhaler not helping.
Inhaler technique reviewed with pt and wife by RN prior to discharge; teach-back adequate.
Discharged HD2 at 14:20, home with wife, ambulatory.
